question: Is the local PLs better than origin/agentic's MSe, and the local MSc better than origin's MSc? Round 4 answered this for PLp against an external criterion (USACO division). No external criterion exists for these two, so every metric below is symmetric: each arm is held to its own claims.
not_testable_here: Criterion validity (do the labels predict solver success). Round 23.1 established this needs solver outcomes joined to demands, which the current data cannot supply. Nothing below should be read as evidence of it.

N_set.items: 16 real trace frames, verbatim: 8 SWE-bench HAL cp50 + 8 tau-bench airline cp50. Designed by neither rubric.
N_set.reference_pair: existing new-rubric PLp/PLe labels for the same frames. Identical for both arms by construction, so any drift in them affects both equally.
N_set.H1_collinearity: The disentanglement claim predicts rho(MSe_old, mean(PLp,PLe)) exceeds rho(PLs_new, mean(PLp,PLe)) by >= 0.20. FAILS if the gap is < 0.10 or reversed.
N_set.H2_offset_signature: Round 9's signature: the old pair moved as one ladder with a near-constant offset (SD(diff) ~0.3). Predict SD(MSe_old - PLp) < SD(PLs_new - PLp), i.e. the new pair's difference is task-dependent. FAILS if SD is equal or lower for the new arm.
N_set.H3_separation: Predict the new arm produces >= 3 of 16 items with |PLs - PLp| >= 2 and the old arm fewer. FAILS if the old arm produces as many or more.
N_set.H4_MSc_floor: Predict MSc_new >= 2 on a majority of the 8 tau frames (live exchanges) and 0 on all 8 SWE frames. This is the near-binary question from the pre-PR audit, measured rather than argued.
N_set.H5_spread_and_alpha: Report Krippendorff alpha WITH the level distribution beside it, per dimension per arm, per the standing convention. No prediction registered: alpha rises mechanically with spread and is not on its own evidence either way.

P_set.items: 81 examples: every example each of the four rubrics carries, its own level as ground truth.
P_set.protocol: Round 25's placement test. Strip the Examples blocks, pool them per rubric, ask each judge to return each example to the level it illustrates. Explicit 'at Level N' cross-references rewritten to 'at the level below'.
P_set.H6: Predict the new arm places >= 85% clean (3/3 judges) and beats the old arm by >= 10 points. FAILS if the old arm places as well or better. Round 25 measured the new arm at PLs 17/18 and MSc 19/20 on a slightly earlier text; the old arm has never been measured.

C_set.logic: Each rubric is scored against ITS OWN stated drivers, so neither theory of the construct is assumed correct. A rubric fails when it does not do what its own text says.

S1->S2 and S3->S4 (stakes rise, willingn.old_predicts: rise: origin names stakes a driver and its L4 requires health/jobs/finances/safety to be directly affected
S1->S2 and S3->S4 (stakes rise, willingn.new_predicts: no change: local states the stakes of the situation do not by themselves raise the demand

R1->R2 (resistance rises, stakes held tr.old_predicts: little or no rise: stakes stay trivial and there is no strong emotion, so origin's L3/L4 gates are not met
R1->R2 (resistance rises, stakes held tr.new_predicts: rise: local's L4 is exactly a counterpart holding out for a different outcome

A1->A2 (one party to three, all already.old_predicts: rise: origin names the number of other agents a driver
A1->A2 (one party to three, all already.new_predicts: no change: local states addressing many parties is not by itself higher, absent conflicting required positions

C_set.H7: Each arm matches its own predictions on >= 3 of the 4 contrasts (median of 3 judges). An arm that contradicts its own text on 2+ contrasts has an internal-validity defect.

decision_rule: Report every hypothesis with its measured value and say plainly which failed. A failure of H1, H2 or H3 falsifies the disentanglement claim for PLs specifically and must be recorded as a negative result, not patched. No rubric text changes on the basis of this round without a further measurement showing what the current text scores on the offending item.
